newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: VA Stahl puts brave face on profit slump.
newsitem.headline: VA Stahl puts brave face on profit slump.

text.p: Austrian steelmaker VA Stahl on Tuesday reported a 48 percent slump in preliminary 1996 net profit and offered little hope for a substantial improvement in the current year, but said 1996 had been a "good year".

Net profit fell to 1.6 billion schillings ($140.1 million) from 3.07 billion a year earlier, hurt by an "overall weak economy and the cyclical downturn" as well as the temporary closure of one of the group's cold-rolling mills, VA Stahl said in a statement.
"For 1997, VA Stahl expects a result at least as good as 1996 because of stabilising market conditions," it added.

Austrian steelmakers have been hit by a change in government tax changes, according to which previously incurred losses are not deductible from 1996 and 1997 profits. VA Stahl itself warned the changes could cost it as much as 450 schillings a year.
Starting this year, VA Stahl plans to reorganise its financial year to begin in April, resulting in a rump 1997 business year from January 1 to March 31.
The company said the dividends for both 1996 and its rump 1997 year would be decided upon at its annual shareholders meeting on June 25. Last year, VA Stahl paid 13 schillings per share.
The company's shares, which were listed on the Vienna stock exchange in October 1995, fell six schillings to close at 408 before the announcement.

VA Stahl is 38.8 percent controlled by Austrian state holding company OeIAG. Engineering group VA Technologie holds 19.05 percent of the shares, while the rest is widely held. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274 ($ = 11.42 Austrian Schillings)
